prospect.name: Jimin Bhuptani
prospect.training_background: Lifting since about age 14, roughly 20 years consistent with occasional three-to-four-month lapses; heavier weightlifting through college, lighter since starting work. Restarted seriously three to four months ago and picked up kettlebells in the last couple of weeks after finding online videos, already reporting fat loss and noticeable results.
prospect.medical: Minor lower back issues attributed to sitting at a desk all day; over 20 years the back was severely painful for roughly one month total, otherwise mild to moderate and never stopping him training. General stiffness from bodybuilding — 'you can't reach too far back because your muscles are too tight'. No other conditions disclosed; none were asked about.

notable.note: Pricing deviation, and the clearest one in this batch. Within roughly 90 seconds of the first price objection — and with no payment plan ever offered — the rep introduced an undisclosed half-price tier: the same six months for $3,000 with Caden doing form checks instead of Trevor. That tier is not in the $6,000/$9,000 offer structure. It reset the anchor mid-call, and the prospect immediately called it 'more palatable', which effectively kills the $6,000 tier for this deal. The rep also garbled the justification — 'That's the reason that that investment is twice as much' — while describing Caden as knowing 'basically everything that Trevor knows', which undermines the premium tier. Separately: the rep never asked what this prospect does for a living, so the primary ICP criterion could not be tested at all. Setter is named as 'Derek', who is not one of the three coded setters; worth checking whether Derek is the person behind the DH code.
